title: Artificial Intelligence in Medical Education
summary: Medical students in their advanced years of study (9th semester or higher) engage in a spoken conversation with a chatbot. During this conversation, they must either deliver a bad diagnosis (e.g., lung cancer, glaucoma/blindness, skin cancer, or Huntington’s disease) or conduct a medical history interview regarding sexuality. Afterward, half of the students receive feedback on their conversation, generated using artificial intelligence. The other half of the students are asked to read through the transcript themselves and reflect on what went well and what did not go as well. Both before and after the conversation with the AI chatbot, the students self-assess how well they performed in delivering bad news or conducting a medical history interview. We are interested in the change in assessment (after minus before) when comparing the groups with and without feedback. Finally, the students in the feedback group indicate how appropriate they find the feedback.
conditions: Medical students solve case studies on the diagnosis and communication of lung cancer, melanoma, Huntington's disease, and sexually transmitted diseases

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Medical students at one of the two universities
- Semester 9 or 10 of medical studies 
- Provided informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Participants who do not fulfill the inclusion criteria
- Participants who do not provide answers to the primary outcome (pre- and post-intervention)
- Participants who indicate repeated participation
- Participants who fail plausibility checks, for example by completing the questionnaire in an unrealistically short time or after a very short interaction with the Chatbot
- Participants who change the conversation topic away from the intended patient-doctor interaction or instances where the AI chatbot malfunctions and deviates
from the conversation (e.g., adopts the physician role instead of the patient role)
- Participants who exclude themselves from participation at the end of the questionnaire
